newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firmer, volume thin ahead of Fed news.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firmer, volume thin ahead of Fed news.

text.p: Irish bonds were slightly firmer on Tuesday in line with other European markets but volumes were thin as investors preferred to sit tight ahead of the FOMC's decision on whether to raise U.S. interest rates, dealers said.
A morning auction by the National Treasury Management Agency of 100 million punts of the 8.25 percent bond due 2015 was covered 1.56 times -- less than anticipated by the market.

"Activity has obviously been damped down ahead of the FOMC meeting," a dealer said. "But otherwise we're still narrowing our spread against Germany in line with a convergence theme in Europe - particularly Italy and Spain."
By 1510 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 15 pence at 102.28 to yield 5.89 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up eight pence at 109.48 to yield 6.59 percent.
The dealer said the market had chased prices up in expectation of good interest in the auctioned paper, with the result that opening levels were less attractive to investors.
The NTMA said the lowest accepted price was 114.26 to give an annual yield of 6.85 percent, while the highest accepted price was 114.47 for an annual yield of 6.83 percent.
The average price was 114.36, giving an annual yield of 6.84 percent.

Meanwhile, Federal Reserve policymakers meet later today to consider raising interest rates for the second time in three months. A narrow majority of top U.S. bond dealers surveyed by Reuters -- 21 out of 39 -- said they expect the central bank to hold rates steady, at least for now.
Those betting on an immediate hike expect the key funds rate would be raised to 5.75 percent from 5.5.
Dealers agreed that whether there is a rate rise or not, Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks about inflation would be carefully scrutinized.
"The market will be anxious to discern how he (Greenspan) is reading inflation, and any clues in that respect will help inform the direction of the market," a dealer said.
